authoritative_sources.title: Canadian Cardiovascular Society Clinical Practice Update on the Assessment and Management of Syncope
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: The CCS guideline library listed this Canadian syncope clinical practice update at retrieval. No newer CCS syncope guideline or CPU was listed; its diagnostic and risk-stratification content remains the current CCS source in the library.

supported_recommendations.statement: For transient loss of consciousness, establish whether the episode is syncope and use a focused history, physical examination, 12-lead ECG, and risk assessment to distinguish likely reflex or orthostatic causes from potentially serious cardiac causes.

source_citations.locator: Initial evaluation, risk stratification, and initial diagnostic work-up

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Not every apparent loss-of-consciousness episode is syncope; seizure, metabolic, toxic, and psychogenic causes require a differential diagnosis when the presentation is inconsistent with transient global cerebral hypoperfusion.

source_citations.locator: Initial evaluation and differential assessment

evidence_boundaries.statement: A normal initial ECG does not by itself exclude a cardiac cause; further investigation is guided by the clinical features and risk assessment rather than routine testing of every patient.

source_citations.locator: Risk stratification and initial diagnostic work-up

evidence_notes: Limited to diagnostic assessment of syncope/loss of consciousness and recognition of cardiac-risk features.

source_citations.locator: Initial evaluation, risk stratification, and initial diagnostic work-up

authoritative_sources.title: 2017 Comprehensive Update of the Canadian Cardiovascular Society Guidelines for the Management of Heart Failure
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: The CCS guideline library continued to list this comprehensive HF guideline at retrieval. Later CCS HF updates address specific therapeutic domains and do not supersede its foundational diagnostic approach.

supported_recommendations.statement: In a patient with peripheral edema, determine whether the distribution and accompanying findings support systemic congestion from heart failure versus a local venous, lymphatic, inflammatory, or other noncardiac cause; assess for associated heart-failure symptoms and signs before attributing edema to cardiac disease.

source_citations.locator: Definition of HF and Diagnosis of HF sections

evidence_boundaries.statement: Peripheral edema alone is not diagnostic of heart failure; its diagnostic value depends on the complete clinical context and corroborating assessment.

source_citations.locator: Definition of HF and Diagnosis of HF sections

evidence_notes: Limited to cardiac differential diagnosis of local/peripheral edema; no treatment recommendation is extracted.

source_citations.locator: Diagnosis of HF section

authoritative_sources.title: 2017 Comprehensive Update of the Canadian Cardiovascular Society Guidelines for the Management of Heart Failure
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: The CCS guideline library continued to list this comprehensive HF guideline at retrieval. Later CCS HF updates address specific therapeutic domains and do not supersede its foundational diagnostic approach.

supported_recommendations.statement: For generalized edema, evaluate for systemic causes including heart failure and integrate history, examination, and appropriate objective assessment for congestion and cardiac structure/function rather than diagnosing heart failure from edema alone.

source_citations.locator: Definition of HF, Diagnosis of HF, and Biomarkers/NPs sections

evidence_boundaries.statement: Generalized edema has systemic noncardiac causes and does not establish a heart-failure diagnosis without compatible clinical and objective findings.

source_citations.locator: Definition of HF and Diagnosis of HF sections

evidence_notes: Limited to cardiac diagnostic reasoning for generalized edema.

authoritative_sources.title: 2020 Canadian Cardiovascular Society/Canadian Heart Rhythm Society Comprehensive Guidelines for the Management of Atrial Fibrillation
authoritative_sources.issuing_organization: Canadian Cardiovascular Society and Canadian Heart Rhythm Society
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: The CCS current guideline library lists the 2020 comprehensive AF guideline; the CCS development page lists a new AF guideline as in development rather than published at retrieval.

supported_recommendations.statement: Evaluate palpitations with a history of episode timing, triggers, associated symptoms, medications and comorbidities, and use ECG documentation or symptom-rhythm correlation to distinguish atrial fibrillation and other arrhythmias from nonarrhythmic symptoms.

source_citations.locator: Chapter 4, Clinical Evaluation; sections 4.1 AF history and 4.2 Investigations

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Palpitations or a perceived irregular rhythm do not establish atrial fibrillation; AF requires electrocardiographic documentation.

source_citations.locator: Chapter 4.2, Investigations

evidence_boundaries.statement: A normal ECG between intermittent episodes does not exclude a paroxysmal arrhythmia; monitoring choice is guided by symptom frequency and the need for symptom-rhythm correlation.

source_citations.locator: Chapter 4.1 AF history and 4.2 Investigations

evidence_notes: Limited to diagnostic assessment of palpitations and rhythm documentation.

source_citations.locator: Chapter 4, Clinical Evaluation

authoritative_sources.title: 2017 Comprehensive Update of the Canadian Cardiovascular Society Guidelines for the Management of Heart Failure
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: The CCS guideline library continued to list this comprehensive HF guideline at retrieval. Later CCS HF updates address specific therapeutic domains and do not supersede its foundational diagnostic approach.

supported_recommendations.statement: When dyspnea may reflect heart failure, assess symptoms and signs of congestion, perform ECG and chest radiography where clinically indicated, and use natriuretic peptides and echocardiography to support or refute the diagnosis and define cardiac structure and function.

source_citations.locator: Diagnosis of HF and Biomarkers/NPs sections

evidence_boundaries.statement: Dyspnea is nonspecific; no single symptom, sign, or test should be used in isolation to diagnose heart failure.

source_citations.locator: Diagnosis of HF and Biomarkers/NPs sections

evidence_notes: Limited to cardiac diagnostic evaluation of dyspnea.

source_citations.locator: Diagnosis of HF and Biomarkers/NPs sections

authoritative_sources.title: 2019 Canadian Cardiovascular Society/Canadian Association of Interventional Cardiology Guidelines on the Acute Management of ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: Focused Update on Regionalization and Reperfusion
authoritative_sources.issuing_organization: Canadian Cardiovascular Society and Canadian Association of Interventional Cardiology
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: The CCS current guideline library lists this Canadian CAD/ACS guideline. The packet uses it only to preserve the diagnostic boundary between chronic stable symptoms and an acute coronary syndrome, not to extract reperfusion treatment guidance.

supported_recommendations.statement: A stable, reproducible exertional chest discomfort pattern suggests chronic coronary syndrome, but a change in frequency, severity, duration, rest symptoms, or associated instability requires assessment for an acute coronary syndrome rather than labeling the presentation stable angina.

source_citations.locator: Guideline scope: acute STEMI assessment and regional reperfusion pathways

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Do not classify new or worsening ischemic symptoms as chronic stable angina without considering acute coronary syndrome and time-sensitive evaluation.

source_citations.locator: Guideline scope and acute STEMI presentation context

evidence_boundaries.statement: An ECG can be normal or nondiagnostic in chronic coronary symptoms; diagnosis integrates pretest likelihood, symptom pattern, and appropriate noninvasive or invasive evaluation.

source_citations.locator: Acute coronary syndrome diagnostic context

evidence_notes: Limited to distinguishing stable coronary symptoms from acute coronary syndrome; no acute treatment directive is extracted.

source_citations.locator: Guideline scope and acute coronary syndrome context

authoritative_sources.title: 2019 Canadian Cardiovascular Society/Canadian Association of Interventional Cardiology Guidelines on the Acute Management of ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: Focused Update on Regionalization and Reperfusion
authoritative_sources.issuing_organization: Canadian Cardiovascular Society and Canadian Association of Interventional Cardiology
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: The CCS current guideline library lists this Canadian CAD/ACS guideline; the library also lists later focused ACS-related antiplatelet and post-ACS pathway resources, neither of which replaces this acute STEMI diagnostic/reperfusion guidance.

supported_recommendations.statement: Suspected acute coronary syndrome requires prompt clinical assessment with 12-lead ECG and cardiac troponin testing, while recognizing that serial testing and the clinical presentation are needed when initial findings are nondiagnostic.

source_citations.locator: Acute STEMI assessment and regional reperfusion pathway context

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: A nondiagnostic initial ECG or troponin result does not exclude acute coronary syndrome when symptoms and risk remain concerning.

source_citations.locator: Acute coronary syndrome presentation and assessment context

evidence_boundaries.statement: ST-elevation MI, non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome, and nonischemic chest pain cannot be distinguished from a single historical feature alone; integrate symptoms, ECG, biomarkers, and serial reassessment.

source_citations.locator: Guideline scope and acute STEMI assessment context

evidence_notes: Limited to ACS diagnostic identification and the need for prompt, serial evaluation; no treatment algorithm is reproduced.

source_citations.locator: Acute STEMI assessment context

authoritative_sources.title: 2017 Comprehensive Update of the Canadian Cardiovascular Society Guidelines for the Management of Heart Failure
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: The CCS guideline library continued to list this comprehensive HF guideline at retrieval. Current 2025 CCS/CHFS HFnrEF guidance covers a treatment phenotype and does not replace the foundational diagnostic section used here.

supported_recommendations.statement: Diagnose heart failure from a compatible syndrome of symptoms and signs together with objective evidence of a structural or functional cardiac abnormality; use natriuretic peptides and echocardiography to support the diagnosis and characterize ventricular function when appropriate.

source_citations.locator: Definition of HF, Diagnosis of HF, and Biomarkers/NPs sections

evidence_boundaries.statement: Heart failure is a clinical syndrome, not a diagnosis made from reduced ejection fraction alone; HF with nonreduced ejection fraction also requires compatible clinical evidence and objective assessment.

source_citations.locator: Definition of HF and Diagnosis of HF sections

evidence_notes: Limited to diagnostic recognition of congestive heart failure and related sleep-disordered-breathing context; no treatment recommendation is extracted.

source_citations.locator: Definition of HF and Diagnosis of HF sections

authoritative_sources.title: 2017 Comprehensive Update of the Canadian Cardiovascular Society Guidelines for the Management of Heart Failure
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: The CCS guideline library retained the comprehensive HF guideline at retrieval; its myocarditis section is the current CCS source located for the diagnostic features in this stable-background packet.

supported_recommendations.statement: Suspect myocarditis with otherwise unexplained myocardial injury or new ventricular dysfunction, particularly when accompanied by chest pain, arrhythmia, heart failure, or cardiogenic shock; evaluate for noninflammatory and ischemic alternatives and use cardiac imaging, including CMR when appropriate, to support diagnosis.

source_citations.locator: Chapter 7.5.5, Myocarditis; recommendations 158 and 161; practical tips

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Normal or low troponin does not rule out myocarditis, and other causes of cardiac dysfunction must be excluded before diagnosing myocarditis.

source_citations.locator: Chapter 7.5.5, Myocarditis; clinical presentation and practical tips

evidence_boundaries.statement: Myocarditis can mimic acute myocardial infarction or pericarditis; the diagnostic label should not be assigned solely from symptoms, ECG, or a biomarker result.

source_citations.locator: Chapter 7.5.5, Myocarditis; clinical presentation and practical tips

evidence_notes: Limited to myocarditis diagnostic suspicion, exclusion of alternatives, and imaging support.

source_citations.locator: Chapter 7.5.5, Myocarditis

authoritative_sources.title: Canadian Cardiovascular Society Clinical Practice Update on Contemporary Management of the Patient With Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: The CCS guideline library lists this 2024 Canadian HCM clinical practice update as the current CCS HCM source at retrieval.

authoritative_sources.title: 2017 Comprehensive Update of the Canadian Cardiovascular Society Guidelines for the Management of Heart Failure
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: The CCS guideline library continued to list this comprehensive HF guideline at retrieval; it supplies the general evaluation boundary for non-HCM cardiomyopathy presentations.

supported_recommendations.statement: Evaluate suspected cardiomyopathy with clinical presentation, family history, ECG, and echocardiography, using cardiac MRI and genetic or specialist evaluation when phenotype or etiology remains uncertain; distinguish hypertrophic, dilated, restrictive, and other myocardial phenotypes from ischemic or valvular disease.

source_citations.locator: Clinical presentation, obstruction assessment, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, and genetic testing sections
Definition of HF and Diagnosis of HF sections

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Unexplained ventricular hypertrophy is not automatically hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; assessment must consider alternative loading conditions and phenocopies, while unexplained ventricular dysfunction also requires evaluation for ischemic and valvular causes.

source_citations.locator: Clinical presentation and diagnostic assessment sections
Diagnosis of HF section

evidence_boundaries.statement: The current Canadian HCM update directly supports hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; this packet does not extend its disease-specific treatment recommendations to dilated, restrictive, or left-ventricular-noncompaction cardiomyopathy.

source_citations.locator: Abstract and scope of the Clinical Practice Update
Definition of HF and Diagnosis of HF sections

evidence_notes: Limited to phenotype-oriented diagnostic assessment of cardiomyopathies. HCM-specific material is sourced from the 2024 CCS update; no disease-specific treatment claim is used for other cardiomyopathy phenotypes.
